title: One-shot sessions, bounded warm pools and runtime MCP presets
requirements: Global defaults and independent agent overrides; existing session policies remain unchanged.
One logical call owns one fresh session; transport retries never create another call or consume another slot.
Per-agent concurrency and aggregate host capacity count starting, idle warm, executing and closing instances.
max_parallel=0 means no pool-specific ceiling; otherwise 0 <= warm_instances < max_parallel. Host capacity always applies; bounded queue and deadlines.
A warm instance has never served another call; each consumed instance is terminated after durable final result.
Queued calls have priority over replenishment; bounded failure backoff prevents launch storms.
Every accepted call has a durable correlated success or error, retried for a disconnected caller.
Errors include code, safe description, stage, started/possible-effect and retry safety; cleanup failure cannot replace success.
Approvals and user input continue the same call; cancellation, timeout and restart settle or recover without unsafe replay.
Normal one-shot closure does not mark agent connection Recovering or disconnect its connector.
Runtime-only MCP preset supports stdio and HTTP, enabled entries and protected host-local secret references.
Inherited harness MCPs plus preset replacements by name plus reserved Nexus integration; no global file edits.
Snapshot preset revision per session; changes affect new sessions and retire incompatible unused warm instances.
Codex, Claude and Pi tool paths preserve Nexus authorization; external MCP permissions remain harness-owned.
Local and remote runtime behavior is equivalent; paths and credentials resolve on the execution host.
UI exposes effective settings, capacity, queue and correlated outcomes; real local validation precedes publication.

steps.deliverable: Validated capacity/preset contracts and migration design
Durable calls, atomic capacity, FIFO queue, deadlines and idempotency
Single-use process preparation, claiming, disposal, backoff and host cap
Host integration, reconciliation and resource accounting
Durable success/error delivery, cancellation and cleanup independence
Storage, merging, credential references and per-harness launch translation
Global/agent overrides, runtime-only MCP editor and capacity visibility
Concurrency, failure, restart, permissions and local/remote harness tests
Domain rules, atomic pool/queue ports and internal durable adapters
Unlimited pool option, isolated opening/ready budgets, compatible UI and lifecycle
Adapter contract, parallel ready work during blocked openings, capacity, timeout, restart, local/remote
Rebuild affected artifacts and verify installed packages; retain explicit live-instance status

release_gate: All steps implemented and tested; unsupported harness behavior is explicit, never silently ignored. No publication requested in this task.
